sanskrit: evaṃ virāgavasanā bahirmālyānulepanāḥ satyaṃ vadata ke yūyaṃ satyaṃ rājasu śobhate
english: Dressed in colourless garments, without garlands or ointments — speak the truth: who are you? Truth is what adorns men among kings.

sanskrit: caityakaṃ ca gireḥ śṛṅgaṃ bhittvā kim iva sadma naḥ advāreṇa praviṣṭāḥ stha nirbhayā rājakilbiṣāt
english: You have broken through the Caityaka peak of the mountain and entered our abode without using a gate, fearless of any offence to the king — what accounts for this?

sanskrit: karma caitad viliṅgasya kiṃ vādya prasamīkṣitam vadadhvaṃ vāci vīryaṃ ca brāhmaṇasya viśeṣataḥ
english: This is the act of one who bears a disguise. What purpose did you have in view? Declare your vigour in speech — especially, what distinguishes a brahmin?

sanskrit: evaṃ ca mām upasthāya kasmāc ca vidhinārhaṇām praṇītāṃ no na gṛhṇīta kāryaṃ kiṃ cāsmadāgame
english: And having thus approached me, why do you not accept the ceremonial welcome offered according to custom? What is your purpose in coming to me?

sanskrit: evam uktas tataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ pratyuvāca mahāmanāḥ snigdhagambhīrayā vācā vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ
english: Thus addressed, Kṛṣṇa of great spirit — eloquent and skilled in discourse — replied in a voice at once warm and grave.

sanskrit: snātakavratino rājan brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā viśaḥ viśeṣaniyamāś caiṣām aviśeṣāś ca santy uta
english: O king, those who follow the snātaka vow — brahmin, kṣatriya, and vaiśya — have rules both particular to each order and rules they share in common.

sanskrit: viśeṣavāṃś ca satataṃ kṣatriyaḥ śriyam archati puṣpavatsu dhruvā śrīś ca puṣpavantas tato vayam
english: The kṣatriya in particular constantly worships Śrī with distinction; and Śrī abides unfailingly where flowers bloom — therefore we wear flowers.

sanskrit: kṣatriyo bāhuvīryas tu na tathā vākyavīryavān apragalbhaṃ vacas tasya tasmād bārhadrathe smṛtam
english: A kṣatriya's valour resides in his arms, not in his words; his speech is therefore restrained — that is the rule remembered, O son of Bṛhadratha.

sanskrit: svavīryaṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ ca bāhvor dhātā nyaveśayat tad didṛkṣasi ced rājan draṣṭāsy adya na saṃśayaḥ
english: The Creator has placed the kṣatriya's true strength in his two arms. If you wish to see it, O king, you shall see it this very day — doubt it not.

sanskrit: advāreṇa ripor gehaṃ dvāreṇa suhṛdo gṛham praviśanti sadā santo dvāraṃ no varjitaṃ tataḥ
english: The righteous always enter an enemy's house by a way other than the door, and enter a friend's house through the proper gate. Therefore we avoided the gate — you are our enemy.

sanskrit: kāryavanto gṛhān etya śatruto nārhaṇāṃ vayam pratigṛhṇīma tad viddhi etan naḥ śāśvataṃ vratam
english: Coming to the house of an enemy on a mission, we do not accept ceremonial honour — know this to be our eternal vow.

sanskrit: jarāsaṃdha uvāca na smareyaṃ kadā vairaṃ kṛtaṃ yuṣmābhir ity uta cintayaṃś ca na paśyāmi bhavatāṃ prati vaikṛtam
english: Jarāsaṃdha said: I cannot recall any enmity that you have created, and even on reflection I see no wrong done to me by you.

sanskrit: vaikṛte cāsati kathaṃ manyadhvaṃ mām anāgasam ariṃ vibrūta tad viprāḥ satāṃ samaya eṣa hi
english: If there is no wrong, how do you regard me as an enemy? Declare that openly, O brahmins — for this is the compact of the righteous.

sanskrit: atha dharmopaghātād dhi manaḥ samupatapyate yo 'nāgasi prasṛjati kṣatriyo 'pi na saṃśayaḥ
english: Indeed, the mind of one who attacks the guiltless is tormented by the destruction of dharma — even if he be a kṣatriya, there is no doubt.

sanskrit: ato 'nyathācaraṃl loke dharmajñaḥ san mahāvrataḥ vṛjināṃ gatim āpnoti śreyaso 'py upahanti ca
english: One who knows dharma and holds great vows, yet acts otherwise in the world, attains the fate of sinners and destroys whatever good he had earned.

sanskrit: trailokye kṣatradharmād dhi śreyāṃsaṃ sādhucāriṇām anāgasaṃ prajānānāḥ pramādād iva jalpatha
english: Knowing that the guiltless are the best among those who walk rightly through the three worlds by the dharma of the kṣatriya, you speak as though in delusion.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca kulakāryaṃ mahārāja kaś cid ekaḥ kulodvahaḥ vahate tanniyogād vai vayam abhyutthitās trayaḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: O great king, the duty of a family is borne by one upholder of that family; yet by its commission we three have risen to this task.

sanskrit: tvayā copahṛtā rājan kṣatriyā lokavāsinaḥ tad āgaḥ krūram utpādya manyase kiṃ tv anāgasam
english: O king, you have seized kṣatriyas who dwell in the world — committing thereby a cruel transgression — yet you consider yourself guiltless?

sanskrit: rājā rājñaḥ kathaṃ sādhūn hiṃsyān nṛpatisattama tad rājñaḥ saṃnigṛhya tvaṃ rudrāyopajihīrṣasi
english: O best of kings, how can a king harm righteous kings? You are seizing those kings in order to offer them to Rudra.

sanskrit: asmāṃs tad eno gaccheta tvayā bārhadrathe kṛtam vayaṃ hi śaktā dharmasya rakṣaṇe dharmacāriṇaḥ
english: That sin committed by you, O son of Bṛhadratha, would fall upon us — for we who walk in dharma are capable of protecting it.

sanskrit: manuṣyāṇāṃ samālambho na ca dṛṣṭaḥ kadā cana sa kathaṃ mānuṣair devaṃ yaṣṭum icchasi śaṃkaram
english: The seizure of human beings as sacrificial victims has never been sanctioned. How then do you wish to worship the god Śaṃkara with human victims?

sanskrit: savarṇo hi savarṇānāṃ paśusaṃjñāṃ kariṣyati ko 'nya evaṃ yathā hi tvaṃ jarāsaṃdha vṛthāmatiḥ
english: Who else would treat men of his own order as sacrificial animals? Only you, Jarāsaṃdha, with your perverted mind.

sanskrit: te tvāṃ jñātikṣayakaraṃ vayam ārtānusāriṇaḥ jñātivṛddhinimittārthaṃ viniyantum ihāgatāḥ
english: We, who follow those in distress, have come here to restrain you — you who cause the destruction of kinsmen — for the sake of the welfare and growth of our kinsmen.

sanskrit: nāsti loke pumān anyaḥ kṣatriyeṣv iti caiva yat manyase sa ca te rājan sumahān buddhiviplavaḥ
english: Your belief that there is no other man among the kṣatriyas of the world equal to you — that too, O king, is a very great confusion of your mind.

sanskrit: ko hi jānann abhijanam ātmanaḥ kṣatriyaḥ nṛpa nāviśet svargam atulaṃ raṇānantaram avyayam
english: What kṣatriya who knows his own lineage would not enter the incomparable, imperishable heaven that follows upon battle, O king?

sanskrit: svargaṃ hy eva samāsthāya raṇayajñeṣu dīkṣitāḥ yajante kṣatriyā lokāṃs tato viddhi magadhādhipa
english: Consecrated to the sacrifice of battle and ascending to heaven itself, kṣatriyas worship the worlds thereby — know this, O lord of Magadha.

sanskrit: svargayonir jayo rājan svargayonir mahad yaśaḥ svargayonis tapo yuddhe mārgaḥ so 'vyabhicāravān
english: Victory is the source of heaven, O king; great glory is the source of heaven; austerity in battle is the source of heaven — this path does not deviate.

sanskrit: eṣa hy aindro vaijayanto guṇo nityaṃ samāhitaḥ yenāsurān parājitya jagat pāti śatakratuḥ
english: This is the victorious quality of Indra, ever present and focused, by which the Hundred-Sacrificed one conquered the asuras and protects the world.

sanskrit: svargam āsthāya kasya syād vigrahitvaṃ yathā tava māgadhair vipulaiḥ sainyair bāhulyabaladarpitaiḥ
english: Who would be so bellicose as you, relying on heaven, proud of the abundance and strength of your vast Magadhan armies?

sanskrit: māvamaṃsthāḥ parān rājan nāsti vīryaṃ nare nare samaṃ tejas tvayā caiva kevalaṃ manujeśvara
english: Do not despise others, O king — valour is not equal in every man; the same energy is not found in any man as in you alone, O lord of men.

sanskrit: yāvad eva na saṃbuddhaṃ tāvad eva bhavet tava viṣahyam etad asmākam ato rājan bravīmi te
english: Only as long as it is not fully understood would this be endurable for you. Therefore, O king, I tell you this.

sanskrit: jahi tvaṃ sadṛśeṣv eva mānaṃ darpaṃ ca māgadha mā gamaḥ sasutāmātyaḥ sabalaś ca yamakṣayam
english: Abandon your pride and arrogance among equals, O Māgadha — do not go with your sons, ministers, and army to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: dambhodbhavaḥ kārtavīrya uttaraś ca bṛhadrathaḥ śreyaso hy avamanyeha vineśuḥ sabalā nṛpāḥ
english: Dambhodbhava, Kārtavīrya, and Uttara Bṛhadratha — these kings who despised their betters perished here along with their armies.

sanskrit: mumukṣamāṇās tvattaś ca na vayaṃ brāhmaṇabruvāḥ śaurirs asmi hṛṣīkeśo nṛvīrau pāṇḍavāv imau
english: Seeking to free those kings from you, we are not those who merely call themselves brahmins — I am Śauri, Hṛṣīkeśa, and these two are the hero Pāṇḍava brothers.

sanskrit: tvām āhvayāmahe rājan sthiro yudhyasva māgadha muñca vā nṛpatīn sarvān mā gamas tvaṃ yamakṣayam
english: We challenge you, O king — stand firm and fight, O Māgadha, or release all the kings; do not go to the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: jarāsaṃdha uvāca nājitān vai narapatīn aham ādadmi kāṃś cana jitaḥ kaḥ paryavasthātā ko 'tra yo na mayā jitaḥ
english: Jarāsaṃdha said: I do not take any kings who are not already conquered. Who has stood against me? Who is there that I have not conquered?

sanskrit: kṣatriyasyaitad evāhur dharmyaṃ kṛṣṇopajīvanam vikramya vaśam ānīya kāmato yat samācaret
english: This is what they call the righteous livelihood of the kṣatriya, O Kṛṣṇa: to subdue by valour and bring under one's sway, then to do as one pleases.

sanskrit: devatārtham upākṛtya rājñaḥ kṛṣṇa kathaṃ bhayāt aham adya vimuñceyaṃ kṣātraṃ vratam anusmaran
english: Having dedicated these kings for the sake of the deity, O Kṛṣṇa, how should I release them out of fear today, mindful as I am of the kṣatriya vow?

sanskrit: sainyaṃ sainyena vyūḍhena eka ekena vā punaḥ dvābhyāṃ tribhir vā yotsye 'haṃ yugapat pṛthag eva vā
english: I shall fight army against army in battle array, or one against one again, or against two or three — simultaneously or one by one.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā jarāsaṃdhaḥ sahadevābhiṣecanam ājñāpayat tadā rājā yuyutsur bhīmakarmabhiḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, Jarāsaṃdha the king, eager for battle and mighty in deed, then commanded the consecration of Sahadeva.

sanskrit: sa tu senāpatī rājā sasmāra bharatarṣabha kauśikaṃ citrasenaṃ ca tasmin yuddha upasthite
english: That king, as battle drew near, O bull of the Bhāratas, remembered Kauśika and Citrasena as his commanders.

sanskrit: yayos te nāmanī loke haṃseti ḍibhaketi ca pūrvaṃ saṃkathite pumbhir nṛloke lokasatkṛte
english: Those two whose names — Haṃsa and Ḍibhaka — had long been spoken of among men in the world, honoured by the world.

sanskrit: taṃ tu rājan vibhuḥ śaurī rājānaṃ balināṃ varam smṛtvā puruṣaśārdūla śārdūlasamavikramam
english: But the mighty Śauri, O king, O tiger among men, remembering that king — best among the strong, his valour like a tiger's —

sanskrit: satyasaṃdho jarāsaṃdhaṃ bhuvi bhīmaparākramam bhāgam anyasya nirdiṣṭaṃ vadhyaṃ bhūmibhṛd acyutaḥ
english: — true to his pledge, Jarāsaṃdha of fearful prowess on earth, assigned as the portion of another to be slain — Acyuta, sustainer of the earth,

sanskrit: nātmanātmavatāṃ mukhya iyeṣa madhusūdanaḥ brahmaṇo ''jñāṃ puraskṛtya hantuṃ haladharānujaḥ
english: — Madhusūdana, the younger brother of the wielder of the plough, the foremost among the self-possessed, did not wish to slay him by his own hand; placing the command of Brahmā first, he deferred the act.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas taṃ niścitātmānaṃ yuddhāya yadunandanaḥ uvāca vāgmī rājānaṃ jarāsaṃdham adhokṣajaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the eloquent Adhokṣaja, the delight of the Yadus, spoke to King Jarāsaṃdha, whose mind was resolute for battle.

sanskrit: trayāṇāṃ kena te rājan yoddhuṃ vitarate manaḥ asmad anyatameneha sajjībhavatu ko yudhi
english: Of the three of us, O king, with which does your mind incline to fight? Let whichever one of us you choose make himself ready for combat.

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa kṛṣṇena yuddhaṃ vavre mahādyutiḥ jarāsaṃdhas tato rājan bhīmasenena māgadhaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Kṛṣṇa, the Māgadha, Jarāsaṃdha of great splendour, chose to fight with Bhīmasena, O king.

sanskrit: dhārayann agadān mukhyān nirvṛtīr vedanāni ca upatasthe jarāsaṃdhaṃ yuyutsuṃ vai purohitaḥ
english: Bearing the choicest remedies, curative preparations, and medicinal herbs, the royal priest approached Jarāsaṃdha who was eager to fight.

sanskrit: kṛtasvastyayano vidvān brāhmaṇena yaśasvinā samanahyaj jarāsaṃdhaḥ kṣatradharmam anuvrataḥ
english: Having performed the rite of benediction through a learned and distinguished brahmin, Jarāsaṃdha — devoted to the duty of the kṣatriya — girded himself.

sanskrit: avamucya kirīṭaṃ sa keśān samanumṛjya ca udatiṣṭhaj jarāsaṃdho velātiga ivārṇavaḥ
english: Removing his crown and smoothing his hair, Jarāsaṃdha rose up like an ocean overflowing its shore.

sanskrit: uvāca matimān rājā bhīmaṃ bhīmaparākramam bhīma yotsye tvayā sārdhaṃ śreyasā nirjitaṃ varam
english: The wise king said to Bhīma of fearful prowess: Bhīma, I shall fight you — it is better to be defeated by a superior than otherwise.

sanskrit: evam uktvā jarāsaṃdho bhīmasenam ariṃdamaḥ pratyudyayau mahātejāḥ śakraṃ balir ivāsuraḥ
english: Having spoken thus, Jarāsaṃdha the enemy-subduer, of great energy, advanced towards Bhīmasena as the asura Bali once advanced against Indra.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃmantrya kṛṣṇena kṛtasvastyayano balī bhīmaseno jarāsaṃdham āsasāda yuyutsayā
english: Then, having taken counsel with Kṛṣṇa and performed the rite of benediction, the mighty Bhīmasena approached Jarāsaṃdha with eagerness to fight.

sanskrit: tatas tau naraśārdūlau bāhuśastrau samīyatuḥ vīrau paramasaṃhṛṣṭāv anyonyajayakāṅkṣiṇau
english: Then those two tigers among men, their arms their weapons, met — both heroes supremely exhilarated, each longing for victory over the other.

sanskrit: tayor atha bhujāghātān nigrahapragrahāt tathā āsīt subhīmasaṃhrādo vajraparvatayor iva
english: From the blows of their arms, from restraints and releases, there arose a tremendous crash like that of thunderbolt against mountain.

sanskrit: ubhau paramasaṃhṛṣṭau balenātibalāv ubhau anyonyasyāntaraṃ prepsū parasparajayaiṣiṇau
english: Both supremely elated, both exceeding strong, each seeking an opening in the other, each desiring victory over the other.

sanskrit: tad bhīmam utsārya janaṃ yuddham āsīd upahvare balinoḥ saṃyuge rājan vṛtravāsavayor iva
english: That dreadful combat, with the crowd driven back, took place in a secluded spot, O king — the clash of those two mighty ones like Vṛtra and Indra.

sanskrit: prakarṣaṇākarṣaṇābhyām abhyākarṣavikarṣaṇaiḥ ākarṣetāṃ tathānyonyaṃ jānubhiś cābhijaghnatuḥ
english: By pulling and dragging, by drawing close and pushing back, they hauled each other about, and struck one another with their knees.

sanskrit: tataḥ śabdena mahatā bhartsayantau parasparam pāṣāṇasaṃghātanibhaiḥ prahārair abhijaghnatuḥ
english: Then, threatening each other with great shouts, they struck each other with blows resembling the collision of boulders.

sanskrit: vyūḍhoraskau dīrghabhujau niyuddhakuśalāv ubhau bāhubhiḥ samasajjetām āyasaiḥ parighair iva
english: Both broad-chested and long-armed, both skilled in wrestling, they locked each other with their arms like iron bars.

sanskrit: kārttikasya tu māsasya pravṛttaṃ prathame 'hani anārataṃ divārātram aviśrāntam avartata
english: The combat began on the first day of the month of Kārttika and went on ceaselessly, without rest, day and night.

sanskrit: tad vṛttaṃ tu trayodaśyāṃ samavetaṃ mahātmanoḥ caturdaśyāṃ niśāyāṃ tu nivṛtto māgadhaḥ klamāt
english: That engagement of the two great souls continued through the thirteenth; but on the night of the fourteenth, the Māgadha withdrew, exhausted.

sanskrit: taṃ rājānaṃ tathā klāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā rājañ janārdanaḥ uvāca bhīmakarmāṇaṃ bhīmaṃ saṃbodhayann iva
english: Seeing the king thus exhausted, O king, Janārdana spoke to Bhīma of terrible deeds, as if awakening him.

sanskrit: klāntaḥ śatrur na kaunteya labhyaḥ pīḍayituṃ raṇe pīḍyamāno hi kārtsnyena jahyāj jīvitam ātmanaḥ
english: An exhausted enemy, O son of Kuntī, cannot be pressed in battle — for one wholly pressed may abandon his own life.

sanskrit: tasmāt te naiva kaunteya pīḍanīyo narādhipaḥ samam etena yudhyasva bāhubhyāṃ bharatarṣabha
english: Therefore, O son of Kuntī, do not press this king to the utmost — fight him evenly with your arms, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa kṛṣṇena pāṇḍavaḥ paravīrahā jarāsaṃdhasya tad randhraṃ jñātvā cakre matiṃ vadhe
english: Thus instructed by Kṛṣṇa, the Pāṇḍava slayer of enemy heroes, having discerned the weak point of Jarāsaṃdha, resolved upon his killing.

sanskrit: tatas tam ajitaṃ jetuṃ jarāsaṃdhaṃ vṛkodaraḥ saṃrabhya balināṃ mukhyo jagrāha kurunandanaḥ
english: Then, to conquer the hitherto unconquered Jarāsaṃdha, Vṛkodara — foremost among the strong, joy of the Kurus — seized him with vigour.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca bhīmasenas tataḥ kṛṣṇam uvāca yadunandanam buddhim āsthāya vipulāṃ jarāsaṃdhajighāṃsayā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Bhīmasena spoke to Kṛṣṇa, the delight of the Yadus, having formed a vast plan with the desire to slay Jarāsaṃdha.

sanskrit: nāyaṃ pāpo mayā kṛṣṇa yuktaḥ syād anurodhitum prāṇena yaduśārdūla baddhavaṅkṣaṇavāsasā
english: This wicked one, O Kṛṣṇa, O tiger among the Yadus, should not be entreated for his life by me — he whose loin cloth is now bound fast.

sanskrit: evam uktas tataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ pratyuvāca vṛkodaram tvarayan puruṣavyāghro jarāsaṃdhavadhepsayā
english: Thus addressed, Kṛṣṇa, that tiger among men, eager for the death of Jarāsaṃdha, replied to Vṛkodara, urging him on.

sanskrit: yat te daivaṃ paraṃ sattvaṃ yac ca te mātariśvanaḥ balaṃ bhīma jarāsaṃdhe darśayāśu tad adya naḥ
english: Whatever supreme divine strength you possess, O Bhīma, and whatever strength of the wind-god — show it to us now, this very day, upon Jarāsaṃdha.

sanskrit: evam uktas tadā bhīmo jarāsaṃdham ariṃdamaḥ utkṣipya bhrāmayad rājan balavantaṃ mahābalaḥ
english: Thus urged, Bhīma the enemy-subduer, of great strength, lifted the mighty Jarāsaṃdha and whirled him about, O king.

sanskrit: bhrāmayitvā śataguṇaṃ bhujābhyāṃ bharatarṣabha babhañja pṛṣṭhe saṃkṣipya niṣpiṣya vinanāda ca
english: Having whirled him a hundredfold with his arms, O bull of the Bhāratas, he broke his back, crumpling and crushing him, and roared aloud.

sanskrit: tasya niṣpiṣyamāṇasya pāṇḍavasya ca garjataḥ abhavat tumulo nādaḥ sarvaprāṇibhayaṃkaraḥ
english: As he was being crushed and the Pāṇḍava roared, there arose a tumultuous sound that struck fear into all living beings.

sanskrit: vitresur māgadhāḥ sarve strīṇāṃ garbhāś ca susruvuḥ bhīmasenasya nādena jarāsaṃdhasya caiva ha
english: All the Māgadhas trembled with fear, and the wombs of women miscarried at the roar of Bhīmasena and the cry of Jarāsaṃdha.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu svid dhimavān bhinnaḥ kiṃ nu svid dīryate mahī iti sma māgadhā jajñur bhīmasenasya nisvanāt
english: "Has the Himālaya split? Is the earth cracking?" — so the Māgadhas understood from the sound of Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: tato rājakuladvāri prasuptam iva taṃ nṛpam rātrau parāsum utsṛjya niścakramur ariṃdamāḥ
english: Then those tamers of enemies left the king at the gate of the royal palace as though he were asleep, casting out his lifeless body by night, and departed.

sanskrit: jarāsaṃdharathaṃ kṛṣṇo yojayitvā patākinam āropya bhrātarau caiva mokṣayām āsa bāndhavān
english: Kṛṣṇa, having yoked Jarāsaṃdha's chariot with its banner and mounted the two brothers upon it, freed the captive kinsmen.

sanskrit: te vai ratnabhujaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ ratnārhaṃ pṛthivīśvarāḥ rājānaś cakrur āsādya mokṣitā mahato bhayāt
english: Those lords of the earth, those kings — freed from great fear — approached Kṛṣṇa who bears jewels, who is worthy of jewels, and paid him homage.
